text:
incident-bot: HIGH PRIORITY: pool-b runtime node-gpu-21 reporting repeated OOMs + elevated 5xx for /chat routes. Paging @mia_oncall, @raj_runtime, @sophia_sre. Duplicate alerts suppressed.

mia_oncall: On-call here, moving to #incident-war-room. Quick status: which tenants impacted and severity?

darya_support: Customer-facing: streamly and bluebox saw spikes in 500s between 1767904200-1767904400, approx 7% error rate for that window. Support tickets opened.

raj_runtime: Uploading immediate logs and allocator dump. Repro window: 1767904180-1767904410. Key log lines:
```
[1767904215] model_worker_4 ERROR: cudaErrorOutOfMemory at alloc_tensor (size=76MB)
[1767904215] model_worker_4 INFO: free_mem=22MB, largest_free=18MB, segments=410
[1767904220] model_worker_9 WARN: retrying request after soft OOM
```
nvidia-smi snapshot from node-gpu-21:
```
| GPU0  40GiB |  Processes: /opt/runtime/serve  38712MiB |
| GPU memory used: 38.2GiB, free: 1.8GiB |
```
Also posting allocator histogram: many sub-1MB bins filled.

carlos_infra: Context: yesterday we enabled aggressive KV prefill for v3.2b on pool-b as part of latency optimization. That prefills per-tenant cache entries onto GPU to reduce cold token latency.

sophia_sre: Initial hypotheses: 1) fragmentation from many tiny KV allocations + kernel alloc pattern in v3.2b (LIKELY). 2) long-lived pinned tensors from third-party ops (POSSIBLE). 3) driver regression (less likely).

mia_oncall: Live mitigations (proposed, ordered):
- A: throttle route concurrency: max_in_flight 32 -> 16 for /chat
- B: set kv_cache_prefill=false for pool-b canary group
- C: soft-evict KV entries older than 10m from GPU to host (if we can)
- D: rolling restart of affected GPU workers to defragment heap
- E: fallback to cpu-backed replica for critical tenants if OOMs persist
Which can we do fast?

raj_runtime: Applying A now: adjusting in-flight config and restarting the per-route controller.
```
curl -s -X POST https://config.internal/v1/routes/chat -d '{"max_in_flight":16}' -H 'Auth: <redacted>'
ops-bot run job/route-controller-reload --pool=pool-b
```
ops-bot: job started job-1767904335.

raj_runtime: Update: after throttle, p99 memory allocation spikes reduced, immediate OOMs dropped to zero but fragmentation warnings still present. Latency increased ~40ms for heavy tenants.

sophia_sre: Good to buy time. Next flip kv prefill off for canary. carlos?

carlos_infra: Flipping kv_cache_prefill=false for canary-pool-b now. Command:
```
PATCH /v1/kvcache/groups/canary-pool-b {"prefill":false}
```
Also enabling soft-eviction policy for prefilled entries older than 600s.

raj_runtime: Observing GPU KV bytes on node-gpu-21 dropping: 30GB -> 18GB over ~70s. Allocator segment count down from 410 -> 260. OOMs have not reappeared in the last 12 minutes.

darya_support: Customer impact: streamly and bluebox errors have dropped to baseline; notifying affected customers with interim update.

mia_oncall: Good. Let's capture timeline for the incident record:
- 1767898000: canary roll of v3.2b began (low traffic)
- 1767901000: v3.2b promoted to pool-b (prefill enabled)
- 1767904180: first OOM alerts seen
- 1767904321: incident page triggered (this thread)
- 1767904335: throttle max_in_flight -> 16 (ops job run)
- 1767904380: kv_cache_prefill=false applied for canary-pool-b
- 1767904460: allocator segments decrease, errors return to baseline

sophia_sre: Vote on hypotheses after mitigations: H1: fragmentation due to many small GPU KV entries + kernel allocs (LIKELY). H2: persistent leak (UNLIKELY based on steady resident set per-process). H3: driver issue (LOW).

carlos_infra: Data: allocator frag index per node-gpu-21 -> 0.92 pre-mitigation, now 0.66. Largest free block increased from 14MB -> 120MB after soft-evictions.

raj_runtime: Repro notes: ran local stress with v3.2b and simulated prefill of 50k small entries (~512KB each). After ~25 minutes fragmentation grows and OOM occurs when batch_size > 10. Repro fixed by either increasing contiguous pool or by coalescing kv entries into fewer larger allocations. Putting repro artifacts in s3://redwood-incidents/1767904321/repro.tar.gz

mia_oncall: Owners & action items (short-term):
- raj_runtime: collect per-process cudaAlloc traces and allocator snapshots and upload (due EOD).
- carlos_infra: add guard in prefill code to not prefill more than 60% device memory and implement per-group threshold (due tomorrow).
- sophia_sre: add rollout advisory: require staged prefill with fragmentation checks and lower default batch sizes when prefill enabled (doc + runbook) (due today).
- darya_support: customer comms follow-up (due today).

carlos_infra: Proposed longer-term remediations:
- move KV cache LRU to host with small GPU hotset for active entries (reduces fragmentation risk)
- allocator improvements: merge small allocations and use slab-like pools for KV objects
- implement on-GPU defragmenter that schedules worker restarts or memory compaction during low traffic windows

raj_runtime: Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/1767904321/{nvidia-smi.log,allocator-dump.json,dmesg.log,repro.tar.gz}. I'll also add a short script to simulate prefill fragmentation in the artifacts.

ops-bot: Incident state: mitigated (degradation resolved). Keeping thread open for RCA follow-ups.

mia_oncall: I'll schedule a 30-45m post-incident review with owners later today. Closing active paging. Please paste any additional traces here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
